# A quick piece of procedural art

<!-- badges: start -->
<!-- badges: end -->

This was Antonio Paez's first contribution to [genuary](https://genuary.art) and it consisted of drawing 10,000 of something.

For this we will use {MexBrewer} and {tidiverse}:
```{r cars}
library(MexBrewer)
library(tidyverse)
```

## Generate the 10,000 objects

We will make 10,000 lines: 5,000 lines are horizontal and of random length in a square with sides measuring 1000 units of length. 

First we will generate the horizontal lines. For this, we will sample randomly from the uniform distribution in the interval [10, 990] for the starting points of the lines. Next, we randomly draw 5,000 values from the uniform distribution, within the interval [x, 1000] for the ending points of the lines (the lines are horizontal, so the y coordinate is a constant). we use the coordinates to define a categorical variable that can be used to assign colors:
```{r}
df_h <- data.frame(x = runif(5000, 
                             min = 10, 
                             max = 950),
                   y = runif(5000, 
                             min = 10, 
                             max = 990)) %>%
  mutate(xend = runif(5000, 
                      min = x, 
                      max = 1000),
         yend = y,
         c = case_when(y < 200 ~ "1",
                       y >= 200 & y < 300 ~ "2",
                       y >= 300 & y < 400 ~ "3",
                       y >= 400 & y < 500 ~ "4",
                       y >= 500 & y < 600 ~ "5",
                       y >= 600 & y < 700 ~ "6",
                       y >= 700 & y < 800 ~ "7",
                       y >= 800 & y < 900 ~ "8",
                       y >= 900 ~ "9"))
```

We repeat the same process, but now for 5,000 vertical lines:
```{r}

df_v <- data.frame(x = runif(5000, min = 10, max = 990),
                   y = runif(5000, min = 50, max = 950)) %>%
  mutate(xend = x,
         yend = runif(5000, 
                      min = x, 
                      max = 1000),
         c = case_when(x < 200 ~ "1",
                       x >= 200 & x < 300 ~ "2",
                       x >= 300 & x < 400 ~ "3",
                       x >= 400 & x < 500 ~ "4",
                       x >= 500 & x < 600 ~ "5",
                       x >= 600 & x < 700 ~ "6",
                       x >= 700 & x < 800 ~ "7",
                       x >= 800 & x < 900 ~ "8",
                       x >= 900 ~ "9"))
```

This gives us 10,000 lines split equally between horizontal and vertical lines. For convenience, we bind the two data frames:
```{r}
df <- rbind(df_h,
            df_v)
```

We will render the lines using `geom_curve` with a small curvature so the lines are not straight. The palettes come from the [{MexBrewer}](https://paezha.github.io/MexBrewer/) package.

## Atentado

```{r 10000-of-something-atentado}
ggplot(df,
       aes(x = x, 
           xend = xend, 
           y = y, 
           yend = yend)) +
  geom_rect(aes(xmin = -200, 
                xmax = 1200, 
                ymin = -200,
                ymax = 1200),
            linewidth = 2.5,
            color = NA,
            fill = mex.brewer("Atentado")[4]) +
  geom_curve(aes(color = c),
             curvature = 0.1,
             linewidth = 0.25,
             alpha = 0.2) +
  coord_equal() +
  scale_color_manual(values = mex.brewer("Atentado", n = 9)) +
  theme_void() +
  theme(legend.position = "none")
```

## Alacena

```{r 10000-of-something-alacena}
ggplot(df,
       aes(x = x, 
           xend = xend, 
           y = y, 
           yend = yend)) +
  geom_rect(aes(xmin = -200,
                xmax = 1200,
                ymin = -200,
                ymax = 1200),
            size = 2.5,
            color = NA,
            fill = mex.brewer("Alacena")[4]) +
  geom_curve(aes(color = c),
             curvature = 0.1,
             linewidth = 0.25,

  coord_equal() +
  scale_color_manual(values = mex.brewer("Alacena", n = 9)) +

```
